title: Claim degenerate delimited tables
lead: The delimited profiler claims three shapes it now rejects as "not a delimited table": a header with no data row, a one-column file, and a file with a row of another width among its first two data rows. Each is described with its evidence (row counts, field counts, the ragged line). **Not in this slice:** new regions or dialects.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A library consumer (a lab sweep-table splitter in another repo) uses squalify as its only describer and must fail or classify these files by its own rules, not lose them at the describe step.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - the delimited profiler and its tests, descriptor docs and the schema if a field changes, README

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A header-only file is claimed: header found, zero data rows.
- A one-column file is claimed with its single field.
- A ragged row among the first two data rows is reported as ragged, and the table is still found.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Build, test and format pass; `slicer check` passes. A release that a consumer can pin follows (owner step).

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: The owner commits. Do not commit; never add Co-Authored-By or similar lines.
